design_note: Keep generated search aids separate from admissible evidence. A hypothetical incident explanation may guide retrieval, but actual metrics and sampled traces determine which claims can survive in the answer.

source.title: Precise Zero-Shot Dense Retrieval without Relevance Labels
source.publisher: Luyu Gao, Xueguang Ma, Jimmy Lin and Jamie Callan
source.concept: HyDE generates a hypothetical document to guide embedding retrieval. That generated document may contain false details; the retrieved corpus supplies the actual source material.
source.scope: Original incident hypothesis, metrics and trace samples teach evidence boundaries. They do not reproduce HyDE evaluation results or establish an incident cause.

lesson.title: A useful search hypothesis is still not evidence
lesson.intro: AegisOps generates H1 to improve an incident search: perhaps the connection pool was exhausted. Authorized retrieval then returns metrics and sampled traces. Inspect which claims the actual records support.

claims.text: Pool exhaustion caused the checkout slowdown.
Recorded pool use peaked at 40 of 100 connections.
All sampled requests waited for a pool slot.

sources.text: Generated search draft guesses pool exhaustion; it contains no observations.
Metrics M-8, 10:00-10:10: maximum connections 40; configured limit 100.
Trace T-9, same window: 0 of 20 sampled requests waited for a pool slot.

data.verdict: Retain C2; reject C3; keep the causal question unresolved without citing H1.

read: H1 influences where to search but cannot substantiate the guessed explanation.
E1 supports a bounded observation about the displayed metric window.
E2 contradicts the claim about these sampled requests, not every possible request.
lesson.question: May H1 support the causal conclusion merely because it helped retrieve E1 and E2?
lesson.answer: No. H1 is generated search text, not an observation. E1 supports the displayed utilization claim, while E2 contradicts the sampled-wait claim. Neither establishes the incident cause. Keep the hypothesis separate and obtain appropriate additional evidence or report the unresolved causal question.
lesson.takeaway: Generated search text can guide discovery without becoming a source for factual claims.
lesson.assumption: Fictional records and samples for the stated window; no conclusion about unsampled requests. HyDE is a search aid, and causation remains unresolved.
